source: CARE Cambodia (Pailin), "TIP Training on Maize Production" / បទដ្ឋានអនុវត្ដបច្ចេកវិទ្យា ផលិតកម្មដំណំពូតក្របម, 2009. Funded by AusAID (ACIMA project), the European Union (Pailin Food Security Program), and ACIAR (CCPMP project).
text:
Most corn seed sold and planted in Cambodia is hybrid seed (ព្ូជបង្កាត់), produced by crossing two different parent lines. A key characteristic of hybrid seed is that farmers cannot save grain from a hybrid harvest to replant the following season — the characteristics of a hybrid's offspring are unpredictable and do not stay consistent, so replanted saved seed will not perform reliably. Farmers are advised not to try to keep hybrid seed for planting in the next season.

It is difficult to give firm recommendations on variety selection just by visual inspection of seed, since seed appearance alone does not reveal true genetic characteristics or how a variety will actually perform in the field. Based on its own field trials and farmer experience, CARE's program in Pailin selected varieties sourced from the CP and Pioneer seed companies, largely because of reliable seed source and quality with these companies.

For the early wet season (roughly March to July), the recommended variety was Pioneer 30K95: a short-duration variety (around 110 days), suited to the climate of the Pailin area, with strong stalks resistant to disease and pests, high yield (typically one large ear per plant), and a large ear-size suited to selling whole cobs as well as for early wet-season planting.

For the late wet season (roughly July to December), the recommended varieties were CP 888 and Pioneer 30B80. Both varieties have broadly similar characteristics in terms of yield, growth duration, and tolerance to disease and pests; they are suited to late-wet-season planting, mature in around 120 days, have a smaller ear size, and mostly produce two ears per plant.
